name: Standing Timber Value Calculator
seoTitle: Standing Timber Value Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: What a standing tree is worth: estimate the board feet in the trunk from its diameter and merchantable height, then apply the price per board foot. Free stand
summary:
What a standing tree is worth: estimate the board feet in the trunk from its diameter and merchantable height, then apply the price per board foot. It returns diameter, volume, volume and value per tree, and the panel shows all of them at once.

It is the number a landowner needs before accepting an offer, and the one a logger uses to decide whether a tree is worth felling. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Standing Timber Value
sections.html:
Volume (m³) = π/4 × (D × taper factor)² × H × 0.42, the form factor of a mature conifer. Board feet = m³ ÷ 0.0023597. Value = board feet × price

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
DBHdiameter at breast height, 1.3 m above the groundcm or in
board foot144 cubic inches of sawn timber, 1 ft × 1 ft × 1 in—
merchantable heightthe usable length of trunkm

sections.title: How do I use the Standing Timber Value?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Measure the diameter at 1.3 m and the merchantable height to the first major fork.
  2. Enter the local price per board foot for the species and grade.
  3. Read the volume in board feet and cubic metres, and the value per tree and for the stand.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: diameter at breast height of 40 cm, merchantable height of 12 m, taper allowance of 10%, price per board foot of 1.2, number of trees of 1.

Substituting them into the formula gives diameter of 15.75 in, volume of 0.5716 m³, volume of 242.23 board feet, value per tree of 290.67, value of the stand of 290.67.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
under 30 cm DBHPolepulp or firewood value, not sawtimber
30 – 50 cmSmall sawtimberthe grade depends on knots and straightness
over 60 cmMature sawtimberworth calling a forester before selling

  • Board-foot rules are regional and approximate. The International ¼-inch rule, Scribner and Doyle each give different answers for the same tree — sometimes by 30%.

  • Diameter is measured at breast height and inside the bark. A quick tape around the trunk gives the circumference, which divides by π to give the diameter.

  • A standing tree is worth much less than its sawn volume: felling, hauling and milling take the majority of the retail price.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Measuring the diameter with the bark on and not subtracting for it, which overstates the volume.
  • Using the total height instead of the merchantable height to the first major fork.
  • Comparing a stumpage (standing) price with a delivered log price, which differ severalfold.

faq.q: How do I measure DBH with a tape?
faq.a: Measure the circumference at 1.3 m and divide by π; a 126 cm circumference is a 40 cm diameter.
144 cubic inches — a piece 1 ft × 1 ft × 1 in thick, the standard unit of sawn timber in North America.

faq.q: Why do two people get different volumes for the same tree?
faq.a: Different board-foot rules. State which one you used before comparing prices.

faq.q: What does the Standing Timber Value actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns diameter, volume, volume and value per tree. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
